name: Schindler R.I.S.E
summary: A self-climbing robot that drills anchor holes and sets bolts for guide rails and shaft doors inside a lift shaft.

germany.statusNote: Not sold as a machine. Schindler uses it itself as part of its own lift installation contracts on high-rise projects, e.g. 030BLN in Berlin (2026). You get it only by ordering Schindler lifts for such a project.

specs.label: Anchor bolts per shaft
specs.conditions: standard shaft; up to 5,000 in high-rise or seismic zones

specs.label: Systems in use
specs.conditions: worldwide; about 40 deployments and over 50,000 anchor bolts by June 2026

notes: Climbs inside the lift shaft by itself; it does not drive on floors.
Measures the shaft walls, detects reinforcement and obstacles, drills and sets bolts around the clock with remote monitoring.
First used as a prototype in 2017; Schindler runs the seven systems itself.
A Schindler operator monitors the work on site by camera.
